description: Atlas-derived whole-body posing specimen with named articulation handles and approximate attached muscle envelopes.
evidence: Teaching geometry. Pose and muscle color do not measure activation or force.
scope: Conservative joint ranges include weighted cervical rotation, skull-on-atlas nod, coupled shoulder elevation and across-chest movement, thoracic turn, pelvic tilt, thumb opposition, finger hinges and spread, hindfoot roll, grouped and individual toe-base motion, jaw opening and small glides, blink, smile and breathing. The teaching rig omits tooth and tissue contact, independent carpal and midfoot glides, toe interphalangeal controls, gaze and tongue control.
knownLimitations: Clearance shapes are fitted to sampled motions. Other combinations can still show muscle overlap or stretch. These shapes do not predict physiological shortening or contact forces.
Shoulder girdle coupling and joint hinges are teaching approximations. Individual anatomy and dynamic recruitment vary.

joints.label: Pelvis
joints.detail: The thigh and trunk orientations are compensated. For the side-tilt comparison the right hip is the support pivot.

joints.label: Thoracic spine
joints.detail: Rotation is distributed through the rib-bearing spine. Compare with the lower-back Trunk control.

joints.label: Neck
joints.detail: C1 turns around the dens of C2. The upper joint receives most of this teaching turn.

joints.label: Upper neck nod
joints.detail: A small skull-on-atlas tilt, with the cervical vertebrae held still.

joints.label: Jaw
joints.detail: Small teaching excursions. The opposite condyle glides forward on a side slide. The disc and tooth contact are outside this model.

joints.label: Right shoulder girdle
joints.coupling: Clavicle and scapula move together as a teaching approximation.

joints.label: Right forearm
joints.detail: The rest hand is already supinated. Increasing this angle pronates; returning toward zero supinates.

joints.label: Right thumb base
joints.detail: Opposition combines palmar lift, movement across the palm and axial rotation of the first metacarpal. This short arc stops before contact.

joints.label: Right thumb MCP
joints.detail: An atlas-fitted hinge approximation; joint surface sliding is not simulated.

joints.detail: Small coupled tibial rotation during the first part of open-chain flexion. The motion illustrates unlocking from full extension.

joints.label: Right hindfoot
joints.detail: Inversion and eversion occur below the talus, not by tilting the tibia. The oblique hindfoot axis and rigid midfoot coupling are teaching approximations; individual joint axes vary.

joints.label: Right toes
joints.detail: The five toe rays move together in this teaching control.

joints.label: Right great toe
joints.detail: The great toe bends independently at the first metatarsophalangeal joint. The group control still moves all five rays.

joints.label: Right second toe
joints.detail: An independent metatarsophalangeal hinge. Digit tendons share some muscle surfaces with the other toes.
